page: Amazon Web Services r3.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor running at 2.5 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The hardware configuration includes 25 MB of L3 cache, standard AVX support, and AES hardware acceleration. Modern instruction extensions such as AVX-512, AMX, and SHA-NI are absent due to the legacy architecture of the Ivy Bridge-EP processor family.

The instance delivers 244.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.62 GB per vCPU. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth measures 110.4 GB/sec, with write bandwidth recording 48.6 GB/sec. For storage, the r3.8xlarge includes 640 GB of local SSD capacity, eliminating external storage overhead for temporary state and fast disk caching. Network connectivity is supported at a baseline rate of 5 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned by default.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate clear architectural tradeoffs. Single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 702.0 and stress-ng single-core performance of 1283.39, rank in the lower quartile of modern cloud benchmarks. However, multi-threaded metrics remain competitive for legacy workloads, evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 6940.0, a PassMark CPU score of 24081.11, and Redis processing capable of 10.08 million SET operations per second.

Given its substantial memory allocation and integrated local SSD, the r3.8xlarge remains practical for memory-bound tasks requiring large operational footprints rather than high per-core compute speeds. Appropriate workloads include in-memory key-value caching such as Redis and Memcached, mid-tier relational database replicas, batch data processing, and enterprise application serving.
description: Amazon Web Services r3.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The server provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, paired with 244.0 GB of RAM, yielding 7.62 GB per vCPU. Storage is addressed through 640 GB of bundled local SSD storage, and networking delivers a baseline throughput of 5 Gbps. Single-core compute scores reflect the older CPU generation, but 32 vCPUs deliver stable multi-threaded throughput, registering 10.08 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark CPU score of 24081.11. The r3.8xlarge is built for memory-heavy environments where high memory density and local scratch disks are critical, making it suitable for distributed in-memory caches, relational database systems, and large-scale data transformation jobs.
